question.text: How are the lights on a traffic signal arranged?

answer.text: Traffic signals usually stand at intersections and stack red on top, yellow in the middle and green at the bottom.

teaching.text: Red sits on top, yellow in the middle and green at the bottom. Remember: Red top, yellow middle, green bottom.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Traffic signals usually stand at intersections and stack red on top, yellow in the middle and green at the bottom.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Red top, yellow middle, green bottom

question.text: What kind of signal do many country intersections have?

answer.text: Many intersections out in the country have only a single yellow or red light.

teaching.text: Out in the country, an intersection may have just one yellow or red light. Remember: Single yellow or red light.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Many intersections out in the country have only a single yellow or red light.

question.text: How do you treat an intersection whose traffic light has no power?

answer.text: If a traffic light has no power or is not working properly, treat the intersection as if it had a stop sign.

teaching.text: No power or a broken light means treat it as a stop sign. Remember: Dark signal, stop sign.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If a traffic light has no power or is not working properly, treat the intersection as if it had a stop sign.

question.text: Is a dark or broken signal handled like a yield sign or a green light?

answer.text: A traffic light that is out or malfunctioning is handled like a stop sign, not like a yield sign or a green light.

teaching.text: A dark signal is never a green light or a yield sign. Remember: Treat it as a stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A traffic light that is out or malfunctioning is handled like a stop sign, not like a yield sign or a green light.

question.text: Whom do you follow when a police officer directs traffic at a signal?

answer.text: When a police officer is directing traffic at a signal, follow the officer's directions.

teaching.text: An officer's directions at a signal come before the light. Remember: Officer over the light.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: When a police officer is directing traffic at a signal, follow the officer's directions.

question.text: What must you do at a steady red light?

answer.text: At a steady red light, stop completely and wait until the light turns green and cross traffic has cleared.

teaching.text: Steady red means stop and wait for green and clear cross traffic. Remember: Stop, wait for green.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a steady red light, stop completely and wait until the light turns green and cross traffic has cleared.

question.text: What must you do at a flashing red light?

answer.text: At a flashing red light, stop completely and then go when it is safe.

teaching.text: Flashing red means stop, then go when it is safe. Remember: Stop, then go when safe.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a flashing red light, stop completely and then go when it is safe.

question.text: How does a steady red differ from a flashing red after you stop?

answer.text: Both a steady red and a flashing red require a full stop, but after a flashing red you may go once it is safe, while after a steady red you wait for green.

teaching.text: Both reds stop you; only the flashing one lets you go before green. Remember: Steady waits; flashing goes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Both a steady red and a flashing red require a full stop, but after a flashing red you may go once it is safe, while after a steady red you wait for green.

question.text: What must you do at a steady red arrow?

answer.text: At a steady red arrow, stop completely and wait for the light to turn green.

teaching.text: A steady red arrow means stop and wait for green. Remember: Stop, wait for green.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a steady red arrow, stop completely and wait for the light to turn green.

question.text: What must you do at a flashing red arrow?

answer.text: At a flashing red arrow, stop completely and then go when it is safe.

teaching.text: A flashing red arrow means stop, then turn when safe. Remember: Stop, then go when safe.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a flashing red arrow, stop completely and then go when it is safe.

question.text: How does a steady red arrow differ from a flashing red arrow?

answer.text: A steady red arrow means stop and wait for green, while a flashing red arrow means stop and then go when safe.

teaching.text: Arrows follow the same steady and flashing pattern as red lights. Remember: Steady waits; flashing proceeds.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A steady red arrow means stop and wait for green, while a flashing red arrow means stop and then go when safe.

question.text: When may you turn right on a steady red?

answer.text: You may turn right on a steady red when it is safe and no sign forbids the turn.

teaching.text: Right on red is fine when safe and no sign forbids it. Remember: When safe, no sign forbids.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may turn right on a steady red when it is safe and no sign forbids the turn.

question.text: When is a left turn on red allowed?

answer.text: A left turn on red is allowed only when you are turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.

teaching.text: Left on red only from a one-way street onto another one-way street. Remember: One-way onto one-way only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A left turn on red is allowed only when you are turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street.

question.text: How do the rules for right on red and left on red differ?

answer.text: Right turns on red are allowed whenever safe and not forbidden by a sign, but left turns on red only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

teaching.text: Right on red is common; left on red is the narrow one-way case. Remember: Right usually; left one-way only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Right turns on red are allowed whenever safe and not forbidden by a sign, but left turns on red only from a one-way street onto a one-way street.

question.text: How must every turn on red begin and end?

answer.text: Any turn on red starts with a full stop; then yield to all traffic and complete the turn staying in your lane.

teaching.text: Every turn on red is stop, yield to all traffic, then turn staying in your lane. Remember: Stop, yield, stay in lane.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Any turn on red starts with a full stop; then yield to all traffic and complete the turn staying in your lane.

question.text: What does a steady yellow light mean, and what should you do?

answer.text: A steady yellow light means red is coming, so slow down and stop before you enter the intersection.

teaching.text: Steady yellow means red is coming, so stop before the intersection. Remember: Red is coming, stop.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A steady yellow light means red is coming, so slow down and stop before you enter the intersection.

question.text: What should you do if the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection?

answer.text: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, do not stop; keep going through.

teaching.text: Already in the intersection when it turns yellow? Keep going. Remember: Already in? Keep going.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If the light turns yellow while you are already in the intersection, do not stop; keep going through.

question.text: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

answer.text: At a flashing yellow light, slow down, look for cross traffic and go ahead with caution.

teaching.text: Flashing yellow means slow, check cross traffic and go carefully. Remember: Slow, check, proceed carefully.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a flashing yellow light, slow down, look for cross traffic and go ahead with caution.

question.text: How does a steady yellow differ from a flashing yellow?

answer.text: A steady yellow means stop before the intersection if you have not entered it, while a flashing yellow means slow down and proceed with caution.

teaching.text: Steady yellow asks you to stop; flashing yellow asks for caution. Remember: Steady stop; flashing caution.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A steady yellow means stop before the intersection if you have not entered it, while a flashing yellow means slow down and proceed with caution.

question.text: What does a steady yellow arrow mean?

answer.text: A steady yellow arrow means the arrow is about to turn red, and you should stop if you can do so safely.

teaching.text: A steady yellow arrow warns that the arrow is about to turn red. Remember: Arrow about to turn red.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A steady yellow arrow means the arrow is about to turn red, and you should stop if you can do so safely.

question.text: What should you do at a flashing yellow arrow?

answer.text: At a flashing yellow arrow, yield before making the turn and then proceed with caution.

teaching.text: A flashing yellow arrow lets you turn only after yielding. Remember: Yield first, then turn.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a flashing yellow arrow, yield before making the turn and then proceed with caution.

question.text: How does a steady yellow arrow differ from a flashing yellow arrow?

answer.text: A steady yellow arrow warns the arrow is about to turn red, while a flashing yellow arrow lets you turn after yielding.

teaching.text: Steady yellow arrow ending, flashing yellow arrow yield and go. Remember: Ending versus yield-and-go.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A steady yellow arrow warns the arrow is about to turn red, while a flashing yellow arrow lets you turn after yielding.

question.text: On a steady green light, whom must you still yield to?

answer.text: A steady green light lets you go through the intersection, but you must still yield to emergency vehicles and others the law requires.

teaching.text: Green lets you go, but emergency vehicles and others still come first when the law says so. Remember: Green still yields.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A steady green light lets you go through the intersection, but you must still yield to emergency vehicles and others the law requires.

question.text: The light turns green while you are stopped. What do you wait for?

answer.text: If you were stopped and the light turns green, let cross traffic clear the intersection before you go.

teaching.text: After stopping, let cross traffic clear before moving on the green. Remember: Let cross traffic clear.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If you were stopped and the light turns green, let cross traffic clear the intersection before you go.

question.text: When may you turn left on a steady green light?

answer.text: On a steady green you may turn left only when it is safe, because oncoming traffic has the right-of-way.

teaching.text: A left turn on a green ball waits for oncoming traffic. Remember: Left on green yields oncoming.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a steady green you may turn left only when it is safe, because oncoming traffic has the right-of-way.

question.text: What does a steady green arrow allow, and what must you still watch for?

answer.text: A steady green arrow lets you turn the way it points with no oncoming or crossing traffic expected, but you still watch for pedestrians.

teaching.text: A green arrow means a protected turn, but pedestrians may still be crossing. Remember: Arrow turn, watch pedestrians.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A steady green arrow lets you turn the way it points with no oncoming or crossing traffic expected, but you still watch for pedestrians.

question.text: How does a left turn on a green ball differ from one on a green arrow?

answer.text: On a steady green ball a left turn must yield to oncoming traffic, while under a green arrow no oncoming or crossing traffic should be moving.

teaching.text: The green ball makes you yield; the green arrow stops oncoming traffic. Remember: Ball yields; arrow protected.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On a steady green ball a left turn must yield to oncoming traffic, while under a green arrow no oncoming or crossing traffic should be moving.

question.text: Does a green light or green arrow mean you never yield?

answer.text: Even on a green arrow you still watch for pedestrians, and even on a steady green you still yield to emergency vehicles.

teaching.text: Green never cancels watching for pedestrians or yielding to emergency vehicles. Remember: Green never ends yielding.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Even on a green arrow you still watch for pedestrians, and even on a steady green you still yield to emergency vehicles.

question.text: What do lines and symbols on the pavement tell you?

answer.text: Lines and symbols on the pavement divide the road into lanes, show where passing and lane changes are allowed and which lanes are for turns, and their color tells you whether the road is one-way or two-way.

teaching.text: Pavement lines show lanes, passing, turns and whether traffic flows one way or two. Remember: Lanes, passing, turns, direction.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Lines and symbols on the pavement divide the road into lanes, show where passing and lane changes are allowed and which lanes are for turns, and their color tells you whether the road is one-way or two-way.

question.text: What do the solid white edge line and the yellow line on your left mark?

answer.text: A solid white line marks the right edge of the travel lane, and a solid or dashed yellow line marks the left edge of the lanes going your way.

teaching.text: White on your right edge, yellow on your left. Remember: White right edge, yellow left.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A solid white line marks the right edge of the travel lane, and a solid or dashed yellow line marks the left edge of the lanes going your way.

question.text: What does a white line separate, and what does the yellow line on your left mark?

answer.text: White lines separate lanes going the same way, while the yellow line marks the left edge of the lanes going your way.

teaching.text: White lines split lanes going your way; yellow marks your left edge. Remember: White same way; yellow left edge.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: White lines separate lanes going the same way, while the yellow line marks the left edge of the lanes going your way.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: White same way; yellow left edge

question.text: May you cross a white dashed line, and what does a white pavement arrow show?

answer.text: White dashed lines separate lanes going the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe, and a white pavement arrow shows the direction that lane must go.

teaching.text: Dashed white may be crossed when safe; arrows show where the lane goes. Remember: Dashed white: cross when safe.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: White dashed lines separate lanes going the same direction and may be crossed when it is safe, and a white pavement arrow shows the direction that lane must go.

question.text: When may you cross a solid white line between lanes?

answer.text: A solid white line between lanes may not be crossed except to avoid a hazard or when you are turning within the next block.

teaching.text: Solid white between lanes is crossed only for a hazard or a turn within the next block. Remember: Hazard or turn just ahead.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A solid white line between lanes may not be crossed except to avoid a hazard or when you are turning within the next block.

question.text: How does crossing a dashed white line differ from a solid white line?

answer.text: A white dashed line may be crossed when safe, while a solid white line between lanes may be crossed only for a hazard or a turn within the next block.

teaching.text: Dashed white invites a safe lane change; solid white says stay. Remember: Dashed yes; solid rarely.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A white dashed line may be crossed when safe, while a solid white line between lanes may be crossed only for a hazard or a turn within the next block.

question.text: Where should you stop at a crosswalk?

answer.text: At a crosswalk, stop with your front wheels just short of the solid white line and never stop on the crosswalk itself.

teaching.text: Stop with your front wheels just before the line, never on the crosswalk. Remember: Before the line, off the crosswalk.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: At a crosswalk, stop with your front wheels just short of the solid white line and never stop on the crosswalk itself.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Before the line, off the crosswalk

question.text: Where are crosswalks found?

answer.text: Crosswalks are usually at intersections but sometimes sit in the middle of a block, and pedestrians there may have their own signals.

teaching.text: Crosswalks are usually at corners but can be in the middle of a block. Remember: Corners, sometimes mid-block.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Crosswalks are usually at intersections but sometimes sit in the middle of a block, and pedestrians there may have their own signals.

question.text: What do solid yellow lines separate, and what do two of them mean?

answer.text: Solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and two solid yellow lines mean neither direction may pass.

teaching.text: Double solid yellow means no passing from either side. Remember: Double yellow, no passing.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, and two solid yellow lines mean neither direction may pass.

question.text: When may you cross a double solid yellow line to turn?

answer.text: You may cross a double solid yellow line to turn into a driveway when it is safe.

teaching.text: A driveway turn is one reason to cross a double yellow. Remember: Into a driveway, if safe.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may cross a double solid yellow line to turn into a driveway when it is safe.

question.text: When may you cross a double yellow to pass, and when may you not?

answer.text: You may also cross it to pass a vehicle moving at less than half the speed limit when safe, but not if that vehicle is farm equipment.

teaching.text: A vehicle under half the limit may be passed when safe, but never farm equipment. Remember: Half-speed vehicle, never farm.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may also cross it to pass a vehicle moving at less than half the speed limit when safe, but not if that vehicle is farm equipment.

question.text: What are the two exceptions to a double solid yellow line?

answer.text: The double yellow exceptions are turning into a driveway and passing a vehicle going under half the speed limit, and the second never applies to farm equipment.

teaching.text: Two narrow exceptions: driveway turns and very slow vehicles that are not farm equipment. Remember: Driveway turns, very slow vehicles.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: The double yellow exceptions are turning into a driveway and passing a vehicle going under half the speed limit, and the second never applies to farm equipment.

question.text: What does a dashed yellow line allow?

answer.text: A dashed yellow line means you may pass when it is safe, while watching for other traffic.

teaching.text: Dashed yellow means you may pass when it is safe. Remember: Dashed yellow, pass if safe.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A dashed yellow line means you may pass when it is safe, while watching for other traffic.

question.text: How does a single dashed yellow line differ from a double solid yellow?

answer.text: A single dashed yellow line allows passing when safe, while two solid yellow lines forbid passing from either side.

teaching.text: Dashed yellow may pass; double solid yellow may not. Remember: Dashed may; double never.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A single dashed yellow line allows passing when safe, while two solid yellow lines forbid passing from either side.

question.text: With a dashed line beside a solid yellow line, who may pass?

answer.text: Where a dashed yellow line runs beside a solid one, only drivers on the dashed side may pass.

teaching.text: Beside a solid line, only the dashed side may pass. Remember: Dashed side passes.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Where a dashed yellow line runs beside a solid one, only drivers on the dashed side may pass.

question.text: With mixed yellow lines, which line decides whether you may pass?

answer.text: With a dashed line beside a solid yellow line, the line nearest you decides: dashed on your side allows passing, solid on your side does not.

teaching.text: Read the line on your own side to decide. Remember: Your side's line decides.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: With a dashed line beside a solid yellow line, the line nearest you decides: dashed on your side allows passing, solid on your side does not.

question.text: What else may mark where passing is allowed?

answer.text: Some passing zones also have signs showing where passing is and is not allowed.

teaching.text: Some passing zones add signs showing where passing is allowed. Remember: Passing zone signs too.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Some passing zones also have signs showing where passing is and is not allowed.

question.text: What is a shared center lane for, and how is it marked?

answer.text: A shared center lane is only for left turns and U-turns, can be used by traffic from either direction, and is marked with white left-turn arrows.

teaching.text: The center lane is for left turns and U-turns from either direction. Remember: Center lane for left turns.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A shared center lane is only for left turns and U-turns, can be used by traffic from either direction, and is marked with white left-turn arrows.

question.text: When may you cross the solid yellow line into a shared center lane?

answer.text: You may cross the solid yellow line into a shared center lane to make a left turn or U-turn, but only enter it when it is safe.

teaching.text: Cross the solid yellow into the center lane only to turn, and only when safe. Remember: Left turn or U-turn, safely.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may cross the solid yellow line into a shared center lane to make a left turn or U-turn, but only enter it when it is safe.

question.text: How are reversible lanes marked and controlled?

answer.text: Reversible lanes run on different hours for each lane, are marked with double dashed yellow lines, and use special overhead lights to show which lanes you may use.

teaching.text: Reversible lanes change by hour and are marked with double dashed yellow lines. Remember: Double dashed yellow, overhead lights.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Reversible lanes run on different hours for each lane, are marked with double dashed yellow lines, and use special overhead lights to show which lanes you may use.

question.text: How do the markings of a shared center lane differ from a reversible lane?

answer.text: A shared center lane is marked with solid and dashed yellow lines and is used only for left turns and U-turns, while a reversible lane is marked with double dashed yellow lines and has different operating hours for each lane.

teaching.text: Solid-and-dashed means center turn lane; double dashed means reversible lane. Remember: Solid-dashed versus double dashed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A shared center lane is marked with solid and dashed yellow lines and is used only for left turns and U-turns, while a reversible lane is marked with double dashed yellow lines and has different operating hours for each lane.

question.text: What do the red X, green arrow and yellow X mean over a reversible lane?

answer.text: Over a reversible lane, a red X means the lane is closed, a green arrow means it is open, and a yellow X means it is changing, so move into a lane with a green arrow.

teaching.text: Over a reversible lane, red X is closed, green arrow is open, yellow X means move to a green lane. Remember: Red closed, green open, yellow leave.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Over a reversible lane, a red X means the lane is closed, a green arrow means it is open, and a yellow X means it is changing, so move into a lane with a green arrow.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Red closed, green open, yellow leave

question.text: Who may use a reserved lane, and how is it often marked?

answer.text: Reserved lanes are only for the type of vehicle named on the sign, are often marked with a white diamond on the sign and pavement, and are illegal to use in any other vehicle.

teaching.text: Reserved lanes belong to the vehicles named on the sign, often marked with a white diamond. Remember: Named vehicles; white diamond.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Reserved lanes are only for the type of vehicle named on the sign, are often marked with a white diamond on the sign and pavement, and are illegal to use in any other vehicle.

question.text: When may other vehicles drive in a reserved lane?

answer.text: You may drive in a reserved lane to turn across it within the next half of a block, and if a bicyclist is in it, move in behind them and turn when safe.

teaching.text: You may enter a reserved lane only to turn within the next half block, behind any bicyclist. Remember: Turning within half a block.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: You may drive in a reserved lane to turn across it within the next half of a block, and if a bicyclist is in it, move in behind them and turn when safe.

question.text: How far ahead must your turn be to enter a reserved lane?

answer.text: A reserved lane may be entered by other vehicles only to turn across it within the next half of a block.

teaching.text: Half a block is the limit for turning through a reserved lane. Remember: Half a block only.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A reserved lane may be entered by other vehicles only to turn across it within the next half of a block.

question.text: What may bus and car pool lane signs list?

answer.text: Signs for bus and car pool lanes may list the days and hours when the restriction applies.

teaching.text: Bus and car pool lane signs may list the days and hours that apply. Remember: Days and hours.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Signs for bus and car pool lanes may list the days and hours when the restriction applies.

question.text: How might bus and bike lanes be marked?

answer.text: Bus and bike lanes may be painted in colors such as red, green or gray; follow the pavement lettering and posted signs.

teaching.text: Bus and bike lanes may be painted red, green or gray; follow the lettering and signs. Remember: Colored paint, read the signs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Bus and bike lanes may be painted in colors such as red, green or gray; follow the pavement lettering and posted signs.

question.text: What is a flex lane, and when is it open?

answer.text: On some highways signs allow the paved shoulder to be used as a flex lane, which is separated by a solid yellow line and opened according to traffic volume and special events.

teaching.text: A flex lane is a shoulder opened by signs, separated by a solid yellow line. Remember: Shoulder opened by signs.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: On some highways signs allow the paved shoulder to be used as a flex lane, which is separated by a solid yellow line and opened according to traffic volume and special events.

question.text: Which vehicles may never use a flex lane?

answer.text: Large trucks may not drive in a flex lane.

teaching.text: Large trucks are never allowed in a flex lane. Remember: No large trucks.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Large trucks may not drive in a flex lane.

question.text: May large trucks use a flex lane when its green arrow is lit?

answer.text: A flex lane is the paved shoulder opened by signs as a travel lane, but large trucks may never use it even when its green arrow is lit.

teaching.text: Even with a green arrow lit, trucks stay out of the flex lane. Remember: Trucks never use it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A flex lane is the paved shoulder opened by signs as a travel lane, but large trucks may never use it even when its green arrow is lit.

question.text: What happens to traffic in a flex lane when there is an incident?

answer.text: If there is an incident along a flex lane, yellow and red X signals tell drivers to merge into the next lane.

teaching.text: An incident on a flex lane brings yellow and red X signals telling you to merge over. Remember: X signals, merge over.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: If there is an incident along a flex lane, yellow and red X signals tell drivers to merge into the next lane.

question.text: What do the green arrow, yellow X and red X mean over a flex lane?

answer.text: Over a flex lane, a green arrow means open, a yellow X means it is closing so merge into the general-purpose lanes, and a red X means closed.

teaching.text: Green arrow open, yellow X closing, red X closed. Remember: Green open, yellow closing, red closed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: Over a flex lane, a green arrow means open, a yellow X means it is closing so merge into the general-purpose lanes, and a red X means closed.
audio_scripts.must_match_memory_hook: Green open, yellow closing, red closed

question.text: How does a yellow X differ from a red X over a flex lane?

answer.text: In a flex lane a yellow X means the lane is closing so you merge into the general-purpose lanes, while a red X means it is already closed.

teaching.text: Yellow X means merge out now; red X means the lane is already closed. Remember: Yellow closing; red closed.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: In a flex lane a yellow X means the lane is closing so you merge into the general-purpose lanes, while a red X means it is already closed.

question.text: What sign marks the end of a flex lane?

answer.text: A Merge sign marks the end of the flex lane, where you merge back into the general-purpose lanes.

teaching.text: A Merge sign marks where the flex lane ends. Remember: Merge sign ends it.

audio_scripts.must_match_card_back: A Merge sign marks the end of the flex lane, where you merge back into the general-purpose lanes.

hooks_spoken: A dark signal is a stop sign, and an officer at a signal outranks it.
Steady red means stop and wait for green; flashing red means stop, then go when safe.
Red arrows follow the same steady and flashing pattern.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of signal basics and red lights. A dark signal is a stop sign, and an officer at a signal outranks it. Steady red means stop and wait for green; flashing red means stop, then go when safe. Red arrows follow the same steady and flashing pattern. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Right on red is allowed when safe and not forbidden.
Left on red only from one one-way street onto another.
Every turn on red starts with a full stop and a yield.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of turning on red. Right on red is allowed when safe and not forbidden. Left on red only from one one-way street onto another. Every turn on red starts with a full stop and a yield. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Steady yellow means stop before the intersection, unless you are already in it.
Flashing yellow means slow and proceed with caution; a flashing yellow arrow means yield first.
A green ball left turn yields to oncoming traffic; a green arrow is protected but still watch for pedestrians.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of yellow and green signals. Steady yellow means stop before the intersection, unless you are already in it. Flashing yellow means slow and proceed with caution; a flashing yellow arrow means yield first. A green ball left turn yields to oncoming traffic; a green arrow is protected but still watch for pedestrians. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: White lines separate lanes going your way; the yellow line marks your left edge.
Cross a dashed white line when safe; a solid white only for a hazard or a turn just ahead.
Stop before the crosswalk line, never on the crosswalk.
recap.narration_text: Time for a quick review of white lines and crosswalks. White lines separate lanes going your way; the yellow line marks your left edge. Cross a dashed white line when safe; a solid white only for a hazard or a turn just ahead. Stop before the crosswalk line, never on the crosswalk. Keep these ideas handy as you practice.

hooks_spoken: Double solid yellow means no passing from either side.
